title: Delete Leaves With a Given Value
summary: Given a binary tree root and an integer target, remove all leaf nodes with the value target.
statement: Given a binary tree root and an integer target, remove all leaf nodes with the value target. Continue removing parent nodes that become leaves with the target value until no such nodes exist.
constraints: Remove every leaf whose value equals target.
A parent that becomes a matching leaf after child removal must also be removed.
Return the remaining tree root, or None if repeated removal deletes it.

reference_solution:
def delete_target_leaves(root,target):
    if root is None:return None
    root.left=delete_target_leaves(root.left,target);root.right=delete_target_leaves(root.right,target)
    if root.left is None and root.right is None and root.val==target:return None
    return root

hints: A parent can become removable only after both children have been processed.
Use postorder recursion and replace each child pointer with its pruned result.
After pruning children, return None exactly when both are absent and the current value equals target.
Postorder repeats the leaf-removal rule upward in one traversal, including deletion of the original root.
editorial: Recursively prune left and right subtrees before testing the current node. This converts the repeated global removal process into one postorder pass: every descendant deletion is already reflected when its parent is evaluated. The oracle independently constructs a separate tree, applies the same declarative fixed-point rule, and serializes the result.

tests.explanation: Removing the original twos makes the left parent two a leaf too, so it is also removed.
Only matching leaves are removed; the nonleaf root value one remains.
